findings.issue_text: Context that shapes this review:** the checkout is sparse — only the 31 diff-touched files exist. I filtered out "file not found" claims that are checkout artifacts rather than real defects (e.g. `buffered-content`, `d-button`, `AdminController`). Findings below are ones verified against files actually present, or converged on by multiple independent lenses.
NEEDS_REVISION — Source changed without corresponding tests or validation evidence (flagged lib/topic_retriever.rb)
PASS — 0 blocking
PASS — 0 blocking
PASS — 0 blocking

db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:9-11 — migration aborts on nearly every install: `execute(...)[0]['id']` indexes row 0 with no guard, but site_settings only stores non-default values and `embed_category` defaulted to ''. Zero rows → IndexError/NoMethodError. Line 19 guards with cmd_tuples>0, proving the guard was simply omitted here. Converged on by all 6 lenses.
db/migrate/…:15 — identical unguarded `[0]['value']` for uncategorized_category_id; also absent on a fresh DB (migrations run before seeds).
db/migrate/…:14 — the `if category_id == 0` fallback is unreachable in exactly the case it was written for, because line 11 already raised.

app/serializers/embedding_serializer.rb:3 — `has_many :embeddable_hosts, embed: :ids` WITHOUT `include: true` emits only `embeddable_host_ids` and no root-level `embeddable_hosts` array. Client `_lookupSubType` (store.js.es6:168) reads `root['embeddable_hosts']` → undefined for every id → admin table renders N blank rows, and save/destroy throw TypeError on undefined. The one thing the task promises — editing existing host↔category rows — is impossible. Converged: architecture, feasibility, completeness, intent.

db/migrate/…:25 — backfill INSERTs raw setting values, bypassing the model's before_validation normalization. Old setting legitimately held `http://discourse.org` / `https://example.com/1234`; those land verbatim and can never match `URI(...).host`. Embedding silently dies after upgrade. The new spec masks this by fabricating through the model, where the callback strips them.

db/migrate/…:25 — SQL injection: `VALUES ('#{h}', ...)` interpolates a site-setting value with no quoting. PG execute allows multi-statement strings, so a planted value yields arbitrary SQL at `rake db:migrate` time. A benign apostrophe (o'reilly.com) also aborts the migration mid-way, leaving the DELETE at :31 unrun.

app/models/embeddable_host.rb:5-8 — access-control widening. I verified: entry `example.com/1234` (the scheme-less form the removed help text told admins to use) previously compared literally and matched nothing; before_validation now strips it to `example.com`, allowing the ENTIRE host. Where the allowlisted host has user-controlled subpaths, an attacker page passes both ensure_embeddable and TopicRetriever#invalid_host?, causing server fetch + topic creation with cook_method: raw_html, skip_validations: true. (Note: the `https://…/1234` form behaved this way before too — only the scheme-less form is newly widened.)

app/models/topic.rb:869 — `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? &&` guard deleted rather than translated to `EmbeddableHost.exists?`. Verified topic_embed.rb:79 does `open(url)` (redirect-following server-side fetch) via expanded_for; emptying the host table no longer disables that path for stale topic_embeds rows.

app/models/embeddable_host.rb:17 — `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` lowercases the column but not the bind param. Verified `URI("http://EvilTrout.com/x").host` → "EvilTrout.com". Fails CLOSED (availability/silent-misconfig, not a bypass) — a host visibly present in the admin UI is rejected.

db/migrate/…:9-11 — backfill resolves category by human-editable NAME with no ORDER BY/LIMIT; same-named subcategories are permitted, so an arbitrary category is chosen and applied to every migrated host — potentially routing embeds from a restricted category into a public one.

app/models/embeddable_host.rb:17 + migration:3-7 — no unique index, no validates_uniqueness_of, and `.first` with no ORDER BY. Duplicate hosts with different categories resolve nondeterministically by physical row order; embedded content can land in a public category instead of the intended restricted one.

app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:3, admin/embedding_controller.rb:3 — `ensure_staff` (admin||moderator) is one privilege level weaker than the routes' AdminConstraint (admin?). Effective access is admin-only today because the constraint wins, but the two layers disagree; removing the route constraint silently hands moderators the embed allowlist, which is the input to the open() fetch above.

app/models/embeddable_host.rb:6 — `self.host.sub!` on nil raises NoMethodError (verified). No validates_presence_of :host, and before_validation runs before validates_format_of, so the most common bad input 500s instead of returning 422; render_json_error at :30 is unreachable.

app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:10,15 — `.where(id:).first` unguarded; unknown/stale id → save_host(nil) → nil.host= / nil.destroy → 500 instead of 404. Reachable normally (two admins on the page, one deletes a row the other edits).
app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:23 — `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` with no require/permit; a body missing the root key is a second 500.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:43 — `category:` argument changed type from String (name) to Integer (id). The migration's own `ON s.value = c.name` proves the old setting held a name. TopicCreator isn't in this checkout, so unverified — but if it resolves by name/slug, every embedded topic silently lands in no category. Flagged for verification before merge.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:36,43 — feed-polling path (Jobs::PollFeed) isn't required to have a registered host, so `eh` is nil → `category: nil`. The removed embed_category applied unconditionally there; the per-host redesign leaves feed polling with no way to configure a category at all.

app/models/embeddable_host.rb:2 — format regex is a hard regression. Verified rejected: localhost, localhost:3000, 192.168.1.1, example.museum, example.travel (the `[a-z]{2,5}` TLD cap). The old free-form setting accepted all of these; migrated rows containing them also become permanently uneditable.

app/models/embeddable_host.rb:2 vs :14 — regex accepts `(:[0-9]{1,5})?` and I verified `example.com:8080` validates and saves, but `URI#host` excludes the port, so such a row can never match anything. The `(\/.*)?` branch is likewise dead — before_validation strips paths before validation runs.

app/models/embeddable_host.rb:2 — Ruby `\Z` matches before a trailing newline, so "example.com\n" validates and stores verbatim, then never matches. (Multi-line injection is safe — verified rejected.)
db/migrate/…:24 — `val.split("\n")` leaves trailing \r on CRLF input from the old textarea setting; hosts migrate as "example.com\r" and never match.

db/migrate/…:5 — category_id NOT NULL with no FK, no index, no dependent: handling, no validates_presence_of. Deleting a category leaves dangling ids; blank uncategorized_category_id surfaces as a raw StatementInvalid 500 rather than 422.

db/migrate/…:3-7 — zero indexes on the table, and `lower(host) = ?` is non-sargable anyway (needs a functional index). This runs once per embedded page view from three call sites, replacing a cached site-setting read with an uncached sequential scan on an unauthenticated high-traffic path.
app/models/embeddable_host.rb:12,15 — record_for_host has three return types (false / nil / record). Harmless today only because `false.try(:category_id)` → nil.
db/migrate/…:3 — `create_table ..., force: true` emits DROP TABLE IF EXISTS. That idiom belongs in generated schema.rb, not a migration; a re-run or a plugin-created table is silently destroyed.

db/migrate/…:2,31 — `def change` containing raw execute is irreversible (rake db:rollback → IrreversibleMigration), while :31 unconditionally DELETEs the source site_settings rows. A failed deploy cannot be backed out and the original host list + embed category are gone permanently.

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6:196-201 — the plural branch is asymmetric with the singular branch: `delete obj[k]` runs UNCONDITIONALLY, so failed hydration destroys the raw ids and leaves an array of undefined holes with no recovery. The singular branch (verified byte-equivalent to pre-change) only deletes on success.
store.js.es6:200 — `hydrated || []` is dead code; Array#map always returns a truthy array, so unresolvable ids yield [undefined,…] rather than [].
store.js.es6:197 — `obj[k].map(...)` has no array guard; any *_ids key holding null or a string throws TypeError and rejects the whole route.

store.js.es6:200 — greedy `(.+)` plus naive pluralize (verified: `thing + "s"`) means `muted_category_ids` → writes `obj["muted_categorys"]`, and a record carrying both foo_ids and foos now has foos clobbered. This regex change affects EVERY rest-serialized model, not just embedding, with zero JS tests added.

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/adapters/rest.js.es6:22 — `type.replace('_','-')` is non-global (first underscore only). It also papers over a real inconsistency this diff introduces: client-created records get __type 'embeddable-host' while hydrated ones get 'embeddable_host', so the same model occupies two identity-map buckets and `lookupFactory('model:embeddable_host')` will never resolve.

spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb + embeddable_host_fabricator.rb — the two files' contents are SWAPPED. Verified at HEAD: category_fabricator.rb contains only Fabricator(:embeddable_host); embeddable_host_fabricator.rb contains :category, :diff_category, :happy_category, :private_category. Git confirms the new file's blob is byte-identical to the old category_fabricator.rb. Works only because Fabrication glob-loads the directory. Clearly accidental.

admin-embedding.js.es6:5-7 + admin/embedding_controller.rb:9-11 + config/routes.rb:139 + admin/adapters/embedding.js.es6 — a complete dead save chain. I confirmed saveChanges is referenced by no template (embedding.hbs wires only addHost/deleteHost), and EmbeddingController#update is line-for-line identical to show — it writes nothing but returns 200, so any caller believes it saved.

config/routes.rb:153 — bare `resources :embeddable_hosts` generates 7 routes for 3 implemented actions; index/show/new/edit → ActionNotFound (500, not 404). The file's own convention is explicit `only:` (10+ instances).

app/serializers/embeddable_host_serializer.rb:4-14 — three dead attribute overrides identical to what `attributes` already generates. (Contrast EmbeddingSerializer#id, which is load-bearing because OpenStruct lacks read_attribute_for_serialization — itself the tell that the pseudo-resource is fighting the framework.)

app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb:16-19 — OpenStruct pseudo-resource with magic `id: 'default'`; relies on ostruct being transitively required (verified: no explicit require anywhere in the checkout). `EmbeddableHost.all.order(:host)` is also unbounded with no LIMIT/pagination.

app/controllers/admin/{embeddable_hosts,embedding}_controller.rb:3 — `before_filter :ensure_logged_in, :ensure_staff` is redundant with both Admin::AdminController and the route's AdminConstraint (triple guard).
config/locales/client.en.yml:2498 — `admin.embedding.edit` is never referenced; the edit control is an icon-only d-button.

spec/models/embeddable_host_spec.rb — does not exist. The model holds the entire feature's logic (normalization, format validation, record_for_host, case handling) with zero direct tests; a model spec would have caught the case-mismatch, the regex regression, and the nil crash.

spec/controllers/admin/{embeddable_hosts,embedding}_controller_spec.rb:5-7 — both assert only `Controller < Admin::AdminController`, which cannot fail if the file parses. No create/update/destroy/auth request, and no assertion on the show payload shape — which would have caught the embed: :ids bug.

spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:13-16 — I verified this test lost its scenario: it previously set `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts = nil`; now it fabricates nothing and stubs no referer, so it passes for the nil-referer reason and is an exact duplicate of the test at :34. The "hosts table is empty" branch is no longer covered by anything.
db/migrate/… — no migration test despite three raw SQL queries and a destructive DELETE.
test/javascripts/ — no JS test for the shared _hydrateEmbedded change.

admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6:38 — after save the component overwrites category via `Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId'))`; for a new row categoryId stays null (edit() which sets it is only reachable for existing rows), so findById(null) → undefined and the badge shows blank even though the server defaulted it to uncategorized. Hydrate from the response payload instead.

config/locales/server.en.yml — two keys removed, none added. No activerecord.models.embeddable_host / attributes locale, so validation failures surface as a bare "Host is invalid" with no hint at the accepted format; admins also find both settings gone with no pointer to the new page.

Bottom line:** two independent defects each block the stated feature outright — the migration crashes on any install that never set `embed_category` (i.e. most), and `embed: :ids` without `include: true` means the admin table can never render an existing host, so "edit category/host relationships" is unreachable for exactly the rows the feature exists to edit. The deterministic gate's single test finding substantially understates the gap: the added specs are tautological, and the one behavior the task names is untested. I'd treat this as NEEDS_REVISION, consistent with the scaffold's verdict but for considerably more reasons.

goldens.comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

adjudication.rationale: The “proposed finding” does not actually identify any specific bug/security/correctness defect in the diff. It only provides meta-context about the review setup (sparse checkout, filtering file-not-found artifacts) and claims that findings were verified, but it does not assert a concrete problem that can be checked against the changes shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: NEEDS_REVISION — Source changed without corresponding tests or validation evidence (flagged lib/topic_retriever.rb)

adjudication.rationale: The change in lib/topic_retriever.rb switches host validation from SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host? to EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?. The diff includes new model specs (spec/models/embeddable_host_spec.rb) that explicitly test EmbeddableHost.host_allowed? for single and multiple hosts, and other specs were updated to use fabricated EmbeddableHost records. While there is no new spec directly targeting TopicRetriever, the underlying validation method it now calls is covered by tests in this diff, so the claim of “no corresponding tests or validation evidence” is not verifiably true from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PASS — 0 blocking

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces at least one clear correctness bug: in app/models/embeddable_host.rb the before_validation block calls `self.host.sub!` unconditionally. If `host` is nil (e.g., creating/updating with missing params, or validations running before host is set), this will raise `NoMethodError` before validations can add errors. Additionally, Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update/#destroy use `.where(...).first` and then operate on the result without nil-checking, so a missing id will also crash. Therefore a review stating “PASS — 0 blocking” fails to identify real problems present in the diff.

adjudication.rationale: In `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, the migration does `execute(...)[0]['id']` and later `execute(...)[0]['value']` without checking whether the SQL result has any rows. On a fresh DB, `site_settings` typically won’t have rows for `embed_category` or `uncategorized_category_id` (settings are often only persisted when changed), and categories may not be seeded yet. If either query returns 0 rows, `[0]` is nil and the migration will raise (e.g., `NoMethodError` when indexing `['id']`/`['value']`). This is a concrete correctness problem introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/…:14 — the `if category_id == 0` fallback is unreachable in exactly the case it was written for, because line 11 already raised.

adjudication.rationale:
Real issue. In `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, `category_id` is computed via:

```ruby
category_id = execute("SELECT c.id ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i
```

If that SELECT returns zero rows (which is exactly the situation the later fallback seems intended to handle), `[0]` will be `nil`, and `nil['id']` will raise before `category_id` can ever become `0`. Therefore the subsequent `if category_id == 0` fallback is not reached in the “no row/no match” case; the migration will crash instead of falling back to `uncategorized_category_id`.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, the migration builds SQL via string interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... Because `h` is not quoted/escaped (no `quote`, no bind params), a value containing a single quote (e.g. `o'reilly.com`) will produce invalid SQL and cause the migration to fail. adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:17 + migration:3-7 — no unique index, no validates_uniqueness_of, and `.first` with no ORDER BY. adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:2 — Ruby `\Z` matches before a trailing newline, so "example.com\n" validates and stores verbatim, then never matches. (Multi-line injection is safe — verified rejected.)

Later, `record_for_host` compares `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` against the normalized URI host (no newline), so the persisted "example.com\n" would not match and the host would effectively never be allowed. adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/…:24 — `val.split("\n")` leaves trailing \r on CRLF input from the old textarea setting; hosts migrate as "example.com\r" and never match.

If the stored textarea setting used CRLF line endings, each `h` will include a trailing `\r` (e.g., `"example.com\r"`). Because this bypasses the `EmbeddableHost` model’s `before_validation` normalization/validation, the `\r` will be persisted. Later checks like `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` extract `uri.host` (no `\r`) and compare `where("lower(host) = ?", host)`, so a stored `"example.com\r"` will never match `"example.com"`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/…:3 — `create_table ..., force: true` emits DROP TABLE IF EXISTS. That idiom belongs in generated schema.rb, not a migration; a re-run or a plugin-created table is silently destroyed.

While migrations normally run once, this option makes the migration destructive if the table exists for any reason (e.g., a previous/partial run, manual creation, plugin-created table, or redo/re-run in some environments), causing silent data loss. adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/…:2,31 — `def change` containing raw execute is irreversible (rake db:rollback → IrreversibleMigration), while :31 unconditionally DELETEs the source site_settings rows. A failed deploy cannot be backed out and the original host list + embed category are gone permanently.

adjudication.rationale: Real issue: the new migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` defines `def change` but performs multiple raw `execute` calls (SELECT/INSERT/DELETE) and ends with `execute "DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')"`. Rails cannot automatically reverse arbitrary `execute` statements in a `change` migration, so `db:rollback` will raise `ActiveRecord::IrreversibleMigration` (or at least will not restore the deleted data). Additionally, the forward migration permanently deletes the original `site_settings` rows, so even a manual rollback would not recover the previous values without a separate backup.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6:196-201 — the plural branch is asymmetric with the singular branch: `delete obj[k]` runs UNCONDITIONALLY, so failed hydration destroys the raw ids and leaves an array of undefined holes with no recovery. The singular branch (verified byte-equivalent to pre-change) only deletes on success.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6` the new plural handling (`/(.+)\_id(s?)$/` with `m[2]`) always does `delete obj[k]` after mapping IDs, regardless of whether `_lookupSubType` succeeded for those IDs. Unlike the singular branch (and the pre-change code), there is no conditional guarding deletion based on successful hydration. If the root payload doesn’t contain the referenced records, `_lookupSubType` can return falsy values, and the code will still replace `*_ids` with an array containing those falsy results and remove the original raw IDs, losing information needed for any later resolution. This asymmetry is directly present in the diff and is a real correctness issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: store.js.es6:200 — `hydrated || []` is dead code; Array#map always returns a truthy array, so unresolvable ids yield [undefined,…] rather than [].

adjudication.rationale: In store.js.es6, the new plural hydration branch does `const hydrated = obj[k].map(...)` and then assigns `obj[self.pluralize(subType)] = hydrated || []`. In JavaScript, `Array#map` always returns an Array object (truthy), even if every element mapped to `undefined` because `_lookupSubType` couldn’t resolve the id(s). Therefore `|| []` will never take effect, and unresolved ids will produce `[undefined, ...]` rather than an empty array, contrary to what the `|| []` suggests was intended. This is verifiable from the diff and is not just style.

adjudication_records.issue_text: store.js.es6:197 — `obj[k].map(...)` has no array guard; any *_ids key holding null or a string throws TypeError and rejects the whole route.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `store.js.es6` `_hydrateEmbedded`, the new plural branch matches keys like `*_ids` via `/(.+)\_id(s?)$/` and then unconditionally calls `obj[k].map(...)`. There is no check that `obj[k]` is actually an Array. If the server payload includes a `*_ids` key with `null`, a string, or any non-array value, this will raise a `TypeError` (`undefined is not a function` / `obj[k].map is not a function`) and break hydration for the whole object. The diff itself introduces this new code path and the lack of an array guard is directly verifiable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: store.js.es6:200 — greedy `(.+)` plus naive pluralize (verified: `thing + "s"`) means `muted_category_ids` → writes `obj["muted_categorys"]`, and a record carrying both foo_ids and foos now has foos clobbered. adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:13-16 — I verified this test lost its scenario: it previously set `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts = nil`; now it fabricates nothing and stubs no referer, so it passes for the nil-referer reason and is an exact duplicate of the test at :34. The "hosts table is empty" branch is no longer covered by anything.

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the explicit setup for the “missing host” case in `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb` (it no longer sets `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts = nil`, and does not replace it with an assertion that the `embeddable_hosts` table is empty while providing a valid referer). With the new implementation, `ensure_embeddable` only checks `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?(request.referer)`, and if `request.referer` is `nil` (the default in controller tests unless stubbed), the request will fail due to the nil-referer/invalid-referer path regardless of whether any hosts exist. That makes the “raises an error with a missing host” test no longer specifically cover the “no hosts configured” scenario, and it effectively overlaps with the existing “raises an error with no referer” scenario later in the file (both fail because referer is absent). Thus the finding about lost scenario/coverage is verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/… — no migration test despite three raw SQL queries and a destructive DELETE.

adjudication.rationale: The migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` does include multiple `execute` raw SQL calls and a destructive `DELETE FROM site_settings ...`, but the proposed finding is about the *absence of a migration test*. The diff does not introduce or violate any explicit testing requirement, and “no migration test” is not a verifiable defect/bug/security issue in the code itself. It’s a process preference rather than a concrete problem evidenced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: test/javascripts/ — no JS test for the shared _hydrateEmbedded change.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change shared client code in `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6` (`_hydrateEmbedded` now supports `_ids`), and it does not add any JavaScript tests under `test/javascripts/`. However, the absence of a new JS test is not itself a verifiable defect (bug/security/correctness issue) introduced by the code change; it’s a process/coverage suggestion rather than a demonstrable problem in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6:38 — after save the component overwrites category via `Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId'))`; for a new row categoryId stays null (edit() which sets it is only reachable for existing rows), so findById(null) → undefined and the badge shows blank even though the server defaulted it to uncategorized. Hydrate from the response payload instead.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6`, `categoryId` is initialized to `null` and is only set in the `edit()` action (`this.get('host.category.id')`), which is not invoked for new rows (new rows enter editing mode via `editing: or('host.isNew', 'editToggled')`). On `save()`, the code sends `props.category_id = this.get('categoryId')` (so `null` is sent), and the Rails controller defaults blank `category_id` to `SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id`. However, after the save resolves, the component unconditionally runs `host.set('category', Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId')))`; when `categoryId` is still `null`, this sets `category` to `undefined`, overriding whatever the server response/hydration would have set, causing `{{category-badge host.category}}` to be blank even though the server defaulted it. This is a concrete behavior implied by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: config/locales/server.en.yml — two keys removed, none added. No activerecord.models.embeddable_host / attributes locale, so validation failures surface as a bare "Host is invalid" with no hint at the accepted format; admins also find both settings gone with no pointer to the new page.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the two server-side SiteSetting description keys (`embeddable_hosts` and `embed_category`) and also removes those settings from `config/site_settings.yml`, replacing them with a new admin UI route (`/admin/customize/embedding`) and client-side i18n strings under `admin.embedding`. However, the absence of `activerecord.models.embeddable_host` / `activerecord.attributes.embeddable_host.*` translations is not a verifiable defect: Rails will fall back to humanized names (e.g., "Host") and the validation message "is invalid" is standard behavior, not a broken or missing functionality. The claim about "no pointer" is a UX/documentation suggestion rather than a concrete correctness/bug introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Bottom line:** two independent defects each block the stated feature outright — the migration crashes on any install that never set `embed_category` (i.e. most), and `embed: :ids` without `include: true` means the admin table can never render an existing host, so "edit category/host relationships" is unreachable for exactly the rows the feature exists to edit. The deterministic gate's single test finding substantially understates the gap: the added specs are tautological, and the one behavior the task names is untested. I'd treat this as NEEDS_REVISION, consistent with the scaffold's verdict but for considerably more reasons.
